ex.s: The research, carried out by scientists at the Columbia Climate School and other institutions, found that if the city maintains past species patterns in new plantings, isoprene production in Manhattan in coming decades will go up by about 140%, and resulting summer ozone levels as much as 30%.
ex.t: 该研究由哥伦比亚气候学院和其他机构的科学家进行,发现如果该市在新栽培中保持过去的物种形态,未来几十年曼哈顿的异丙烯产量将上升约140%,从而导致夏季臭氧水平高达30%.

ex.s: Scientists at Salk Institute are making use of the natural capacity of plants to absorb carbon dioxide by enhancing their root systems.
ex.t: 萨尔克研究所的科学家正在利用植物的自然能力,通过增强根系吸收二氧化碳。

ex.s: To design these climate-saving plants, the scientists are using a research tool called SLEAP — an AI software that tracks multiple features of root growth.
ex.t: 为了设计这些节省气候的植物,科学家们正在使用一个叫做SLEAP的研究工具——一个跟踪根生长的多种特征的AI软件.

ex.s: Now, Pereira has teamed up with plant scientist Professor Wolfgang Busch to apply SLEAP to plants.
ex.t: 现在,佩雷拉与植物科学家沃尔夫冈·布施教授合作,将SLEAP应用到植物上.

ex.t: SLEAP会帮助科学家做什么?

ex.s: Computer programming is a must for scientists.
ex.t: 计算机编程对科学家来说是必不可少的.

ex.s: Even bottled water, scientists found earlier this year, contains 10 to 1,000 times more microplastics than originally thought.
ex.t: 甚至瓶装水,科学家今年早些时候发现的,包含的微塑料比原先想象的多10到1000倍.

ex.s: Scientists are still trying to determine how harmful microplastics are — but what they do know has raised concerns.
ex.t: 科学家仍在试图确定微塑料的危害程度——但他们知道什么引起了人们的关切。

ex.s: “The way they demonstrated how microplastics were trapped through the boiling process was nice,” Caroline Gauchotte-Lindsay, an environmental engineer of the University of Glasgow in Scotland who was not involved in the research, tells New Scientist.

ex.s: In the race to document the species on Earth before they go extinct, researchers and citizen scientists have collected billions of records.
ex.t: 在灭绝前记录地球上的物种的比赛中,研究人员和公民科学家收集了数十亿的记录.

ex.s: This makes sense because the people who get observational biodiversity data on mobile devices are often citizen scientists recording their encounters with species in areas nearby.
ex.t: 这样做是有道理的,因为在移动设备上获得观测生物多样性数据的人往往是公民科学家,记录他们在附近地区与物种的遭遇.

ex.s: Give guidance to citizen scientists.
ex.t: 指导公民科学家.

ex.s: One doubter about the safety of cloud seeding is Chuck Doswell, a research scientist who just retired from the University of Oklahoma.
ex.t: 一个对云种子安全性的怀疑者是刚刚从俄克拉何马大学退休的研究科学家查克·多斯韦尔.

ex.s: Many scientists shared the commonsense expectation that as permafrost melted, lakes would at first expand with meltwater flowing into them.
ex.t: 许多科学家都抱有共同的期望,即随着永久冻土的融化,湖泊最初会随着融水的流入而扩大。

ex.s: Scientists have labeled this phenomenon “disastrous lake loss”
ex.t: 科学家将这一现象称为“令人厌恶的湖泊丧失”。

ex.s: Why did scientists miss this?
ex.t: 科学家为什么错过这个?

ex.s: When I decided to pursue a postgraduate degree, I wanted to develop a novel research programme and quickly establish myself as an independent scientist.
ex.t: 当我决定攻读研究生学位时,我想开发一个小说研究计划,并迅速确立自己独立科学家的地位.

ex.s: By learning when to ask for help, I eventually found myself on the way to becoming an independent scientist.
ex.t: 通过学习什么时候求救,我最终发现自己在成为独立科学家的路上.

ex.s: Recently, scientists have started a debate on _______the computers will “think” like human in half a century.
ex.t: 最近,科学家们开始了一场关于计算机在半个世纪里将像人类一样“思考”的辩论。

ex.t: 教授给艺术家和工程师,但很少教授给科学家。

ex.s: But using machine learning and artificial intelligence, some scientists propose that human diets consist of at least 26,000 biochemicals—and that the vast majority are not known.This shows that we have some way to travel before achieving the first objective of systems t hinking - which,in this example, is to identify more constituent parts of the nutrition system.
ex.t: 但利用机器学习和人工智能,一些科学家提出人类的饮食至少包括26,000个生化物质 — — 而绝大多数是未知的。 这表明,我们在实现“吸食系统”这一首要目标之前有某种途径可以旅行 — — 在这个例子中,这是为了确定营养系统中更多的组成部分。

ex.s: One is computer scientist Chris Johnson who I see as someone who helps keep the field honest The other is physicist Philip Taylor.

ex.s: Some scientists insist that once we discover the truth about the world, we are done.
ex.t: 有些科学家坚持认为,一旦我们发现了世界的真相,我们就完成了。

ex.s: The history of science offers many examples of matters that scientists thought they had resolved, only to discover that these matters needed to be reconsidered.
ex.t: 科学史提供了科学家认为已经解决的问题的许多例子,只是为了发现这些问题需要重新考虑.

ex.s: Other scientists may say scientific findings are true because they use “the scientific method.” But we can never actually agree on what that method is.
ex.t: 其他科学家可能认为科学发现是真实的,因为他们使用“科学方法 ” 。 但是,我们永远无法就这种方法究竟是什么达成一致。

ex.s: Recently a leading scientist said the scientific method was to avoid fooling oneself into thinking something is true that is not.
ex.t: 最近一位著名科学家说,科学方法是 避免自欺欺人 认为某事是真实的。

ex.s: Scientists have bitterly argued about which methods are the best, and, as we all know, bitter arguments rarely get resolved.
ex.t: 科学家们苦恼地争论了哪种方法是最好的,我们都知道,苦恼的论点很少得到解决。

ex.s: They seldom cause arguments among scientists.
ex.t: 它们很少引起科学家的争论。

ex.s: Scientists: Defenders of Science
ex.t: 科学家:科学卫士

ex.s: Scientists with new perspectives.
ex.t: 有新视角的科学家.

ex.s: Discover how architects, product designers and scientists use similar skills in their work.
ex.t: 发现建筑师,产品设计师和科学家在工作中如何使用类似的技能.

ex.s: Why do we dream？Scientists aren't completely sure,and they have diverse____11____ (idea)．Dreams might be a side effect of memory making.When you sleep,your brain sorts through everything ____12____ happened during the day，trying to link new experiences to old memories.As it ____13____ (connect) things，your brain tums them into a story,and you get a dream．
ex.t: 为什么我们做梦?科学家们并不完全肯定,他们有多样化的 11 (idea). 梦想可能是记忆制造的副作用. 当你睡觉时,你的大脑在白天发生了一切的 12 ,试图将新的经验与旧的记忆联系起来. 因为 13 (连接)的东西,你的大脑把它们打成一个故事,而你得到一个梦.

ex.s: Hundreds of scientists, writers and academics sounded a warning to humanity in an open letter published last December: Policymakers and the rest of us must engage openly with the risk of global collapse.
ex.t: 数百名科学家、作家和学者在去年12月发表的公开信中向人类发出了警告:决策者和我们其他人必须公开参与应对全球崩溃的风险。

ex.s: A survey of scientists found that extreme weather events, food insecurity, and freshwater shortages might create global collapse.
ex.t: 对科学家的调查发现,极端天气事件、粮食无保障和淡水短缺可能导致全球崩溃。

ex.s: Time is a major concern of philosophers and scientists．
ex.t: 时间是哲学家和科学家们主要关注的问题.

ex.s: Scientists think this is the plants' way to prevent the spread of any tree diseases and make life more difficult for leaf-eating insects like caterpillars.
ex.t: 科学家认为这是植物防止任何树病传播的方法,使食叶昆虫如毛虫的生活更加困难.

ex.s: Scientists in Louisiana were so concerned that they decided to pay hunters $5 a tail.
ex.t: 路易斯安那州的科学家们非常担心,以至于他们决定给猎人每尾巴5美元.

ex.s: Then, on two separate morning visits to the scientists’ lab, each man walked for an hour at an average speed that, in theory should allow his body to rely mainly on fat for fuel.
ex.t: 然后,在两次对科学家实验室的单独上午访问中,每人步行一个小时的平均速度,从理论上讲,这应该允许他的身体主要依靠脂肪作为燃料.

ex.s: Just before and an hour after each workout, the scientists took additional samples of the men’s blood and fat tissue.
ex.t: 科学家在每次锻炼前一小时采集到更多男性血液和脂肪组织样本。

ex.s: In looking into the stories of biological discovery, I also began to find something else, a collection of scientists, usually brilliant occasionally half-mad, who made the discoveries.
ex.t: 在研究生物发现的故事时,我也开始找到其他的东西, 科学家们的集合, 通常是聪明的偶尔半疯狂的, 他们做出了这些发现。

ex.s: The results held true even after the scientists accounted for the participants’ overall health status.
ex.t: 即使在科学家对参与者的总体健康状况作了说明之后,结果还是真实的。

ex.s: Mathematical models have also revealed that food webs may be unstable， where small changes of top predators can lead to big effects throughout entire ecosystems． In the 1960s， scientists proposed that predators at the top of a food web had a surprising amount of control over the size of populations of other species﹣including species they did not directly attack．
ex.t: 数学模型也揭示出食物网可能不稳定,其中顶层捕食者的小变化会导致整个生态系统的巨大影响. 20世纪60年代,科学家提出食物网顶端的捕食者对包括它们没有直接攻击的物种在内的其他物种的种群数量拥有惊人的控制量.
